gloss: at hand; on hand; close by

definitions.explanation: The area near one's hands or within easy reach.
What one currently has in their possession, especially money or materials.
The way one uses their hands, especially in skilled work.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}に{辞書|じしょ}がある。
examples.english: I have a dictionary at hand.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}に{資料|しりょう}がないので、{後|あと}で{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.english: I don't have the materials at hand, so I'll check later.

examples.japanese: {携帯|けいたい}をいつも{手元|てもと}に{置|お}いている。
examples.english: I always keep my phone close at hand.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}の{現金|げんきん}が{足|た}りない。
examples.english: I don't have enough cash on hand.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}に{残|のこ}った{貯金|ちょきん}は{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: The savings I have left on hand are small.

examples.japanese: {今月|こんげつ}は{出費|しゅっぴ}が{多|おお}くて、{手元|てもと}にほとんどお{金|かね}がない。
examples.english: I spent a lot this month and have almost no money on hand.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}が{狂|くる}ってコップを{落|お}としてしまった。
examples.english: My hand slipped and I dropped the cup.

examples.japanese: {手元|てもと}が{暗|くら}くて、{細|こま}かい{作業|さぎょう}がしにくい。
examples.english: It's dark where my hands are, so it's hard to do detailed work.

notes:
USAGE PATTERNS:
・{手元|てもと}に〜がある - to have something at hand
・{手元|てもと}に〜がない - not to have something at hand
・{手元|てもと}が{狂|くる}う - one's hand slips, to fumble

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{手元|てもと}{不如意|ふにょい} - being short of money
・{手元|てもと}を{離|はな}れる - to leave one's hands (possession)
・{手元|てもと}に{届|とど}く - to arrive at hand

RELATED:
・{手持|ても}ち - what one has on hand
・{身近|みぢか} - close at hand, familiar
・{近|ちか}く - nearby
